name: EML Parser
description: Parse the headers, body parts and attachments of an EML message.

results.name: Field name
results.truncated: Content dropped because it exceeded the limit

hints.input: Paste the `.eml` source, or drop a message file to fill it in automatically.
hints.encoding: The charset of the source text; body parts are actually decoded with the charset declared in `Content-Type`.
hints.maxAttachmentBytes: Per attachment byte limit. 0 uses the server default of 10 MB, and the maximum is 50 MB.
hints.output: Headers keep their original order so the `Received` chain stays readable, and RFC 2047 encoded words are decoded.

faq.q: Why is the header order preserved?
faq.a: The standard library stores headers in a map, which loses the order. The tool parses the raw text itself, so the `Received` chain still reads correctly.
No. Attachments only come back in the response as base64; the server neither writes them to disk nor logs or caches them.

faq.q: What if the body text looks garbled?
faq.a: Body parts are decoded with the charset declared in `Content-Type`. When the declaration is missing or unknown the text is treated as UTF-8, and undecodable bytes become U+FFFD.
